chapter: Small groups, Europe and Kansas City memories (repeated passages)
title: Talented players stuck in big bands without solos
summary: They talk about Charlie Parker's time in Kansas City bands and how many talents never get a chance to solo.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: I guess when you were in Kansas City, Bird hadn't come on the scene.
No, he hadn't. He was with...what band...? I don't remember... Was it Kirk? Was it Andy Kirk's band?
He was with Jay McShann, but that was...
He was with Harlan Leonard after he took the Rockets.

Yeah. But I think he was... He must have been with Kirk. But he wasn't playing like that. He was just... I guess maybe he was one of those kind of guys I've been trying to tell you about being stuck in a band and never get no chance to play nothin'. And then, when he did get a chance, the guys found out what kind of guy he was! That's all. You know, there's so much talent hidden in these big bands that don't get a chance; they don't get a chance to play. They just sit up there and play what the music is. Of course, they're getting a little experience from it. But some guys, they're gonna get experience and never nothing happens. You know? So you have to get an outside job. That's what so many guys have had to do; they get outside jobs, you know. So many of them. You know what I mean?
